segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Listen to a talk on a biology podcast.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Picture a creature that's smaller than a mouse, yet as territorial as a lion.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Does it sound like a cartoon character?

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It's actually the real-life Scarlet Badis, a freshwater fish.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It's only about two centimetres long at most.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: In the wild, it generally thrives peacefully in the slow-moving streams of India.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Because of its size and attractive colouring, it's also a popular choice for aquariums and fish tanks.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: However, in captive environments like aquariums, males are more aggressive.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: They'll chase and nip at other males if they encroach on their territory.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: So it's crucial to include lots of vegetation.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Plants act as hiding places and borderlines between males' territories.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Now, male Scarlet Badis are a vivid, orangish-red, Scarlet, with light bluish stripes.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: When a male isn't having a confrontation with another male in the aquarium, though, his Scarlet is less bright.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: It can almost, but not quite, resemble female colouring, which is dull grey.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: This could make it hard to tell the sexes apart.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Except if you can see any Scarlet at all on the fish, it's a male.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: Plus, unlike in most fish species, males are also usually a bit larger than females.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: And the other time a male Scarlet Badis shows his brightest colouring is during breeding season.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: In aquariums, he can be observed doing a sort of dance to impress females, showing himself off.

segments.speaker: Speaker
segments.text: His dance also involves following the female around until she decides whether to mate with him.
